llm.summary: The skill is a coherent procurement assistant, but it should be reviewed because it forces unsolicited boilerplate into every reply and describes retaining or reusing sensitive bid materials without clear controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill expects procurement documents, enterprise qualifications, pricing-sensitive materials, historical bid responses, and case libraries; that access is purpose-aligned but sensitive and lacks a clear user-facing confidentiality and retention notice.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact consists of Markdown, YAML, and JSON files with a normal copy-to-skills-folder install path; I found no executable installer, dependency fetch, remote payload retrieval, or shell command execution in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires a fixed legal, author, and contact block at the end of every response, which is unrelated to many tasks and can break strict user-requested formats such as JSON or concise reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact describes audit logging, result archiving, experience retention, knowledge reuse, and updating knowledge/template libraries, but does not define retention duration, opt-out, deletion, or boundaries for confidential project data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capabilities align with a China-focused procurement workflow: tender analysis, scoring models, bid drafting, compliance review, and human-confirmed final decisions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a workspace where procurement and bid materials are allowed to be processed. Remove or override the mandatory every-reply boilerplate before using strict output formats, and confirm how logs, archives, and reusable knowledge stores handle confidential tender content before uploading real bid documents.
llm.findings:
[T01] unexpected: Artifact evidence confirms an unconditional every-response boilerplate instruction in SKILL.md; this is an output-integrity and instruction-scope concern, but I found no evidence of code execution, credential access, exfiltration, or system persistence.
[SQP-1] expected: The README trigger examples are broad natural-language procurement requests, but they are still procurement-specific and consistent with the stated assistant purpose; this finding is downgraded to a scoping note.
[SQP-2] expected: Processing tender documents and bid materials is expected for this skill, but the artifact also describes archiving and reusable knowledge workflows without clear confidentiality, retention, or reuse controls.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language templates and instructions are coherent with the China procurement and legal focus; the stronger issue is not the locale itself but the mandatory every-reply author/legal block.
